title: Elastic Commitment Protocol for Throughput Guarantees
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines an elastic commitment protocol — the end-to-end provisioning workflow, approval matrix, and capacity-planning primitives that let customers request throughput guarantees with an adaptive buffer for bursty traffic. The goal is to reduce friction for sales/onboarding while protecting fleet utilization and preserving predictable SLOs for existing customers.

Scope and motivation:
- Intake: a compact form for sales/solutions to capture expected p95 latency target, steady-state RPS, burst RPS, burst duration distribution, preferred regions, retention/window for commitment, and billing preference (commit/payg/hybrid).
- Approval: automated scoring (risk/ops cost), manual gate for >X GPU-hours/week or >$Y/month, and a lightweight escalation path for unusual constraints (SLA length >12 months, air-gapped network).
- Provisioning: temporary shadow allocation (commitment runway) that reserves capacity while final verification runs (canary canary) and model compatibility checks happen.
- Autoscaling policy tie-in: map commitment level to autoscale targets and a dynamic buffer (percent + absolute token runway) to support bursts without violating latency SLOs.
- Fleet controls: tenant-rebalancer, graceful overcommit bands, and preemption policy when capacity constraints are tight.

Design decisions and trade-offs so far:
- Buffering model: we decided to combine a percentage buffer (default 20%) with a time-windowed absolute cap for short bursts. Trade-off: percentage protects steady-state but can blow up cost for long tails; the time-windowed cap prevents runaway billing during long sustained bursts.
- Approval automation threshold: initial heuristic is 3x steady->burst ratio or >2M tokens/day. Engineering asked to surface historical traffic patterns from similar tenants to improve accuracy; agreed as follow-up (ENG-63421).
- Canary vs preallocated shadow: we will allocate a soft shadow pool (unbilled until commit is final) to perform automated validation. This adds complexity in bookkeeping but reduces failed provisionings.
- Pricing coupling: PM recommends a small surcharge for elastic buffer usage above the guaranteed baseline to disincentivize permanent overcommit. Finance is in review.

Required artifacts and links:
- Intake form spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Elastic+Commitment+Intake+Spec
- Intake mockups (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Elastic-Onramp-Mocks
- Approval scoring alg (doc): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Commitment+Scoring+V1
- Autoscale mapping prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4512
- Telemetry dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/throughput/elastic-commit-ops
- Incident learning that motivated runway feature: https://postmortem.redwood.ai/2025-11-dedicated-burst-failure

Operational workflow (high level):
1) Sales creates intake via form -> automated pre-check (quota/risk) -> creates PM review task if flagged.
2) For auto-approve: allocate shadow capacity and run compatibility + canary traffic for 2 hours.
3) If canary passes and billing terms accepted, convert shadow to committed capacity and schedule rollout (canary -> ramp -> fully routed).
4) For manual-approve cases: Operations reviews estimated fleet impact (automated cost delta + suggested queuing window) and either approve, request adjustments, or reject.
5) Post-commit: system monitors burst adherence and will trigger suggested config changes (buffer sizing, model quantization recommendation) via Optimize recommendations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form implemented and validated with 3 pilot customers.
- Automated scoring runs and flags correctly for 90% of historical test cases used in training set.
- Shadow allocation bookkeeping prevents double-counting of GPU capacity and shows correct projected cost delta in console.
- Autoscale mapping prototype integrated with routing rules and tenant-rebalancer hook.
- Playbook documented: approval steps, rollback, and escalation contacts.

Open questions / next steps:
- Buffer default tuning: start at 20% + 10k tokens for 60s window; run 2 pilot customers to validate. (Owner: Diego)
- Finalize surcharge rates with Finance and Legal — target decision by 2026-03-20. (Owner: Maya)
- Engineering scope split: ENG-63421 (scoring infra), ENG-63422 (shadow allocation bookkeeping), ENG-63423 (tenant-rebalancer preemption rules).
- UX: DES-4001 to produce intake UX and the console rollout flow.

Long-form rationale and unusual constraints:
Some enterprise customers have highly bursty traffic tied to end-of-month batch processes or user-driven spikes. The naive approach of hard-reserving peak capacity is costly and causes utilization inefficiencies. The elastic commitment protocol aims to provide predictable guarantees for steady-state throughput while providing a controlled, billable runway for bursts. We prioritize preserving latency SLOs over absolute utilization maximization when customers opt-in for guarantees.

Compliance and security notes:
- Private/on-prem reservations with air-gapped networking will require manual approval and on-site validation (flagged in approval scoring as high-risk).
- No new customer data collection is introduced by intake; all sample canary traffic must be synthetic unless customer explicitly permits sample recordings.

Notes from stakeholder review (2026-03-10):
- Legal: confirm contract language for buffer billing.
- Finance: provide model for expected ARR uplift vs. unit cost increase from buffer guarantees.
- Sales: want a streamlined 2-minute intake flow for >$10k/month deals; anything longer will hinder conversion.
